messages:
alice: FYI customer Aurora on Dedicated pool dp-42 is seeing a sudden spike in TPS and getting 429s. Root says 'burst credits exhausted' and responses failing assertion checks. Anyone looking?
lee: I see the alert from the admission-controller: 
```
[2026-03-17T14:01:12Z] admission: deny request customer=aurora pool=dp-42 reason=burst_credits_exhausted current_tps=1540 limit_tps=500 burst_headroom=0
[2026-03-17T14:01:12Z] serve: fallback_policy=reject
```
michael: Oof. Is this noisy neighbor or legit spike? Aurora says they ran a marketing send and projected 400 tps but hit 1500.
support-ops: Aurora CS confirms they flipped a batch job that fan-outed many generation calls. They've attached a curl repro.
aurora-cs: repro (sanitized):
```
for i in {1..2000}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer x...' -d '{"model":"redwood-large","prompt":"x","max_tokens":64}' & done
```
lee: That's an all-at-once fanout, so admission control correctly rejected most and returned 429s. But latency also spiked on the pool, so some customers saw 500s.
alice: Customer is upset because they were billed for retries and saw degraded UX. They want emergency capacity and an explanation.
michael: Quick questions: what are dp-42 autoscale min/max replicas and burst_credits config?
sre-bot: dp-42 config: min_replicas=1 max_replicas=12 scaling_policy=queue_latency target_rps=300 burst_credits=1200 (tokens) current_replicas=1
lee: Burst credits 1200 tokens is low for 1500 tps burst. Also min_replicas=1 meant cold start/queueing.
support-ops: Proposed mitigation plan: 1) temporarily increase burst_credits for dp-42 to 6000 2) bump min_replicas to 3 3) enable soft-fallback model redwood-small for Aurora only 4) ask customer to throttle to 200 tps via client-side backoff.
alice: Can infra do (1)+(2) quick? This is a paying customer on Dedicated.
lee: I'm spinning a quick override: `kubectl -n dedicated patch cm dp-42 --patch '{"data":{"burst_credits":"6000","min_replicas":"3"}}'` — doing now.
[system]: deploy-bot: config updated for dp-42 by lee.
michael: Also enabling an admission-controller emergency-rule to allow Aurora up to 800 tps for the next 15m while capacity ramps: `admission policy add --customer aurora --allow-tps 800 --duration 15m`
support-ops: Applied. Noting this will consume burst credits fast.
aurora-cs: After your changes we see errors drop from 74%->18% and latency 95th from 1100ms->420ms. Thanks. But their engineering wants a durable plan so this doesn't recur.
alice: We need a post-incident action: headroom plan for Dedicated pools per customer, and per-customer burst budget alerts before exhaustion. Also update onboarding doc so Dedicated customers get recommended client-side rate limits when sending bulk jobs.
lee: Agreed. Suggest change: set pool default min_replicas=2 for production customers and auto-escalate min_replicas when sustained queue depth > 10 for >2m.
michael: Also recommend sku-level reservations: customers can purchase extra burst_credits pool or configure per-route queueing with token-bucket.
support-ops: I'll open a ticket with incidence notes and timeline and assign AC & Infra to implement the runbook changes. Ticket: RFC-2891.
sre-bot: Alert summary: incident_id=inc-20260317-aurora duration=22m peak_tps=1620 errors=429,500 mitigation=burst_credits_increase,min_replicas_bump,admission_exception
aurora-cs: Thanks team — Aurora will rate-limit the fanout immediately and wants a follow-up meeting about guaranteed headroom.
alice: Ownering follow-up: michael to own pool policy changes, lee to own infra default config, support-ops to schedule postmortem with Aurora next week.
michael: I'll draft the headroom calc: recommended burst_credits = expected_peak_tps * 5 + baseline_pool_latency_margin. Share tomorrow.
lee: Closed the emergency override. Keeping monitoring on for 2h.
[reaction] :thumbsup: from aurora-cs
